ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Natsume Sōseki Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient visit for three weeks of epigastric pain with black stools and iron-deficiency anemia, with urgent gastroenterology referral for endoscopy. Concerns: He has had stomach pain for weeks and his stools turned black; he wants to know whether it is cancer; He needs to finish the serial he is writing and fears that illness will stop him. [S]

Vonoprazan 20 mg oral tablet, one tablet by mouth each morning for eight weeks for gastric ulcer healing
One tablet each morning for eight weeks

Vonoprazan 20 mg oral tablet, one extra tablet by mouth each evening for 14 days during eradication therapy (20 mg twice daily with the morning dose)
One tablet each evening for 14 days

Two capsules three times daily for 14 days

tr.td: New patient visit for three weeks of epigastric pain with black stools and iron-deficiency anemia, with urgent gastroenterology referral for endoscopy
Gastroenterology consultation with upper endoscopy and biopsy, diagnosis of gastric ulcer, and start of vonoprazan and iron
Two-week review: biopsy results, Helicobacter pylori resistance testing, and start of eradication therapy
Eleven-week review: urea breath test, repeat endoscopy for ulcer healing, anemia, and surveillance planning
Same-day sick visit for acute low back strain, managed without NSAIDs

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Initial evaluation and safety: blood count, iron studies and metabolic panel; Glasgow-Blatchford score; stop ibuprofen and all NSAIDs and use acetaminophen; urgent upper endoscopy within three days; no acid-suppressing medicine or antibiotic before the biopsies unless bleeding recurs; call 119 or go to the emergency department at once for black or bloody stools, vomiting blood or coffee-ground material, fainting, or severe pain

Urgent gastroenterology consultation for upper endoscopy with biopsy within three days, to find the cause of the bleeding, exclude gastric cancer, test for Helicobacter pylori, and advise on treatment

Iron-deficiency anemia: oral iron once the source is found at endoscopy; blood count about four weeks after starting iron and then every three months for a year; continue iron about three months after the hemoglobin is normal and until ferritin is replete; colonoscopy if the anemia does not correct once the ulcer has healed
Stress and sleep: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and at the end of the episode; regular meals, a fixed bedtime, and writing hours that leave the evening free; counselling if scores rise

Gastric ulcer and Helicobacter pylori: vonoprazan 20 mg each morning for eight weeks; eradication chosen by the biopsy resistance result (vonoprazan 20 mg twice daily with amoxicillin 1 g three times daily for 14 days for a clarithromycin-resistant strain); 13C urea breath test at least four weeks after the antibiotics and two weeks after vonoprazan; repeat endoscopy with biopsy of the scar at about ten weeks

Gastric cancer surveillance after eradication: upper endoscopy yearly because of moderate atrophy with intestinal metaplasia in the antrum (OLGA stage II), lifelong; no smoking, little alcohol and less salt

Acute low back strain: stay active, superficial heat, gentle stretching, and acetaminophen up to 3 g a day for a few days; no ibuprofen, naproxen, aspirin or other NSAID, including topical or combination cold remedies, while the ulcer heals and preferably for good; finish the eradication course; return for leg weakness, numbness in the saddle area, loss of bladder or bowel control, fever, or pain that is not easing in four weeks
Prediabetes: walking at least 150 minutes a week, regular meals with less refined rice and sweets, and weight kept steady; repeat A1c in three months once iron is replete, then yearly
Endoscopy within three days of the first visit, with cancer excluded by biopsy
Endoscopy three days after the first visit; margin biopsies benign at two weeks
No further bleeding and no emergency admission through the episode
No further black stools or vomiting of blood; no admission
Helicobacter pylori eradicated, confirmed by urea breath test
Urea breath test negative seven weeks after therapy
Gastric ulcer healed at repeat endoscopy
Healed to a white scar at repeat endoscopy; scar biopsies sent
Hemoglobin normal and ferritin above 50 ng/mL
Hemoglobin 14.0 g/dL; ferritin 46 ng/mL, iron continuing
